The teams ranked first through fourteenth of the [[2009 Chinese Super League|previous season]] and two promoted teams from the [[2009 China League One|2009 League One season]] participated in this season. [[Shandong Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng]] won the title for third time in seven years. == Promotion and relegation == '''Teams promoted from [[2009 China League One]]''' * [[Liaoning F.C.|Liaoning The most high profile of these were the former Head of the [[Chinese Football Association]] Nan Yong, his deputy Yang Yimin and Zhang Jianqiang who used to be in charge of referee arrangements.{{cite web |url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english2010/china/2010-01/22/c_13146975.htm |title=Chinese soccer chief sacked after being questioned by police |access-date=2010-02-24 |archive-date=2010-01-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100125215147/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english2010/china/2010-01/22/c_13146975.htm |url-status=dead }} The crackdown quickly discovered that [[Guangzhou F.C.|Guangzhou GPC]] and [[Chengdu Tiancheng F.C.|Chengdu Blades]] had both bribed their way into the top tier. Both were relegated to the second tier and did not appeal, making their punishment the harshest dealt out to a club.{{cite web|url=http://english.peopledaily.com.cn/90001/90779/90871/6902886.html|title = China goes further to fight football match-fixing - People's Daily Online}} In keeping the top table at 16 teams, [[Zhejiang Professional F.C.|Hangzhou Greentown]] and [[Chongqing Liangjiang Athletic F.C.|Chongqing Lifan]] both retained their places within the top tier despite being originally slated for relegation.{{cite web|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/j/2010-02-24/11214853407.shtml|title=天上掉馅饼重庆力帆偷着乐 狂喜之外更感到自身差距_国内足坛-甲A_NIKE新浪竞技风暴_新浪网|website=sports.sina.com.cn|access-date=12 March 2019}} ==
